_meta.title: Surah At-Takwir (81)
_meta.description: Surah At-Takwir, The Folding Up: phrase meanings, tafsir and Arabic vocabulary.

q1.question: What does the Arabic phrase إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ in the surah mean?
options: When the oceans are set ablaze
When the sun is folded up
q1.explanation: إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ means 'When the sun is folded up,' roots ش-م-س (sun) and ك-و-ر (fold) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q2.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَإِذَا النُّجُومُ انكَدَرَتْ mean?
options: And when the seas burst forth
And when the graves are overturned
And when the sky is torn
q2.explanation: وَإِذَا النُّجُومُ انكَدَرَتْ means 'And when the stars fall,' roots ن-ج-م (stars) and ك-د-ر (fall/dim) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q3.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَإِذَا الْجِبَالُ سُيِّرَتْ mean?
options: And when the winds are unleashed
And when the mountains are set moving
And when the earth is shaken
And when the sun is darkened
q3.explanation: وَإِذَا الْجِبَالُ سُيِّرَتْ means 'And when the mountains are set moving,' roots ج-ب-ل (mountains) and س-ي-ر (move) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q4.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَإِذَا الْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ mean?
options: And when pregnant camels are neglected
And when wild beasts are gathered
And when the sky is stripped away
q4.explanation: وَإِذَا الْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ means 'And when pregnant camels are neglected,' roots ع-ش-ر (camels) and ع-ط-ل (neglect) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q5.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَإِذَا الْوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ mean?
options: And when the birds fly away
And when the wild beasts are gathered
And when the cattle are slaughtered
And when the oceans are filled
q5.explanation: وَإِذَا الْوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ means 'And when the wild beasts are gathered,' roots و-ح-ش (beasts) and ح-ش-ر (gather) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q6.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ mean?
options: And when the seas are frozen
And when the oceans are set ablaze
And when the rivers dry up
q6.explanation: وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ means 'And when the oceans are set ablaze,' roots ب-ح-ر (seas) and س-ج-ر (blaze/fill) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q7.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَإِذَا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ mean?
q7.explanation: وَإِذَا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ means 'And when souls are paired,' roots ن-ف-س (souls) and ز-و-ج (paired) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q8.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَإِذَا الْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ mean?
options: And when the buried daughter is asked
And when the newborn child is questioned
And when the mother is interrogated
And when the orphan is recompensed
q8.explanation: وَإِذَا الْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ means 'And when the buried daughter is asked,' roots و-أ-د (buried alive) and س-أ-ل (asked) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q9.question: What does the Arabic phrase بِأَيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ mean?
options: For what crime she was forgiven
For what sin she was killed
For what wealth she was exiled
For what speech she was blamed
q9.explanation: بِأَيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ means 'For what sin she was killed,' roots ذ-ن-ب (sin) and ق-ت-ل (killed) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q10.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَإِذَا الصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ mean?
options: And when the scrolls are hidden
And when the records are rolled up
And when the pages are spread open
And when the books are burned
q10.explanation: وَإِذَا الصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ means 'And when the pages are spread open,' roots ص-ح-ف (pages) and ن-ش-ر (spread) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q11.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ كُشِطَتْ mean?
options: And when the sky is stripped away
And when the sky is painted
And when the sky is rebuilt
And when the sky is opened
q11.explanation: وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ كُشِطَتْ means 'And when the sky is stripped away,' roots س-م-و (sky) and ك-ش-ط (strip off) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q12.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَإِذَا الْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ mean?
q12.explanation: وَإِذَا الْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ means 'And when Hellfire is ignited/blazed,' roots ج-ح-م (Hell) and س-ع-ر (ignite) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q13.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَإِذَا الْجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ mean?
options: And when Paradise is brought near
q13.explanation: وَإِذَا الْجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ means 'And when Paradise is brought near,' roots ج-ن-ن (Paradise) and ز-ل-ف (bring near) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q14.question: What does the Arabic phrase عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا أَحْضَرَتْ mean?
options: Every soul will know what it has left behind
Every soul will know what it has brought forth
Every soul will know what it has forgotten
Every soul will know what it has inherited
q14.explanation: عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا أَحْضَرَتْ means 'Every soul will know what it has brought forth,' roots ع-ل-م (know), ن-ف-س (soul), ح-ض-ر (bring/present) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q15.question: What does the Arabic phrase فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ mean?
options: So I swear by the retreating stars
So I swear by the bright morning
So I swear by the soaring birds
So I swear by the flowing rivers
q15.explanation: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ means 'So I swear by the retreating stars,' roots ق-س-م (swear) and خ-ن-س (retreat/hide) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q16.question: What does the Arabic phrase الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ mean?
q16.explanation: الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ means 'The running and hiding/sweeping stars,' roots ج-ر-ي (run) and ك-ن-س (hide/sweep) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q17.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا عَسْعَسَ mean?
options: And by the night when it departs/darkens
And by the night when it is bright
And by the night when it is short
And by the night when it is calm
q17.explanation: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا عَسْعَسَ means 'And by the night when it departs or darkens,' roots ل-ي-ل (night) and ع-س-ع-س (darken/retreat) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q18.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ mean?
options: And by the dawn when it breathes/brightens
And by the dawn when it fades
And by the dawn when it is cold
And by the dawn when it storms
q18.explanation: وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ means 'And by the dawn when it breathes (begins to shine),' roots ص-ب-ح (morning) and ن-ف-س (breathe) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q19.question: What does the Arabic phrase إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ mean?
options: Indeed, it is the word of a poet
Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger
Indeed, it is the word of a soothsayer
Indeed, it is the word of a wise king
q19.explanation: إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ means 'Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger (Jibril),' roots ق-و-ل (word), ر-س-ل (messenger), ك-ر-م (noble) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q20.question: What does the Arabic phrase ذِي قُوَّةٍ عِندَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ مَكِينٍ mean?
options: Possessor of power and high status with the Owner of the Throne
Possessor of wealth and authority among men
Possessor of knowledge and books on earth
Possessor of strength and armies in battle
q20.explanation: ذِي قُوَّةٍ عِندَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ مَكِينٍ means 'Possessor of power, secure with the Owner of the Throne,' roots ق-و-ي (power), ع-ر-ش (throne), م-ك-ن (status) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q21.question: What does the Arabic phrase مُطَاعٍ ثَمَّ أَمِينٍ mean?
q21.explanation: مُطَاعٍ ثَمَّ أَمِينٍ means 'Obeyed there (in the heavens) and trustworthy,' roots ط-و-ع (obeyed) and أ-م-ن (trustworthy) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q22.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَمَا صَاحِبُكُم بِمَجْنُونٍ mean?
options: And your companion is not a poet
And your companion is not mad
And your companion is not a liar
And your companion is not a sorcerer
q22.explanation: وَمَا صَاحِبُكُم بِمَجْنُونٍ means 'And your companion (Prophet Muhammad) is not mad,' roots ص-ح-ب (companion) and ج-ن-ن (madness) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q23.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالْأُفُقِ الْمُبِينِ mean?
options: And certainly he saw him in the clear horizon
And certainly he heard him in the silent night
And certainly he knew him in the city
And certainly he followed him in the cave
q23.explanation: وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالْأُفُقِ الْمُبِينِ means 'And certainly he saw him (Jibril) in the clear horizon,' roots ر-ؤ-ي (see), أ-ف-ق (horizon), ب-ي-ن (clear) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q24.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ mean?
options: And he is not a keeper of secrets
And he is not withholding concerning the unseen
And he is not neglectful of the message
And he is not doubtful of the revelation
q24.explanation: وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ means 'And he is not withholding/greedy concerning the unseen,' roots غ-ي-ب (unseen) and ض-ن-ن (withhold) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q25.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَيْطَانٍ رَّجِيمٍ mean?
options: And it is not the word of an expelled devil
And it is not the word of an evil king
And it is not the word of a false prophet
And it is not the word of a straying poet
q25.explanation: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَيْطَانٍ رَّجِيمٍ means 'And it is not the word of an accursed/expelled devil,' roots ش-ي-ط (devil) and ر-ج-م (stoned/expelled) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q26.question: What does the Arabic phrase فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ mean?
q26.explanation: فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ means 'So where are you going?' roots ذ-ه-ب (go) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q27.question: What does the Arabic phrase إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعَالَمِينَ mean?
options: It is not except a warning for the inhabitants
It is not except a reminder to the worlds
It is not except a story for the nations
It is not except a law for the believers
q27.explanation: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعَالَمِينَ means 'It is not except a reminder to the worlds,' roots ذ-ك-ر (reminder) and ع-ل-م (worlds) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q28.question: What does the Arabic phrase لِمَنْ شَاءَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ mean?
options: For whoever among you wills to be guided
For whoever among you wills to take a right course
For whoever among you wills to gain wealth
For whoever among you wills to be patient
q28.explanation: لِمَنْ شَاءَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ means 'For whoever among you wills to take a right course (be steadfast/straight),' roots ش-ي-ء (will) and ق-و-م (straight/steadfast) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

q29.question: What does the Arabic phrase وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ mean?
options: And you do not will except that Allah wills
And you do not know except what Allah teaches
And you do not act except what Allah commands
And you do not speak except what Allah permits
q29.explanation: وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ means 'And you do not will except that Allah wills,' roots ش-ي-ء (will) and أ-ل-ه (Allah) (Quran.com, Ibn Kathir).

q30.question: What does the Arabic phrase رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ mean?
q30.explanation: رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ means 'The Lord of the worlds,' roots ر-ب-ب (Lord) and ع-ل-م (worlds) (MyIslam, Al-Maududi).

iq1.question: Surah At-Takwir is classified as which type of surah according to its place of revelation?
options: Revealed during the migration to Abyssinia
iq1.explanation: Surah At-Takwir is a Makkan surah focusing on cosmic signs of the Day of Judgment, accountability, and the divine authenticity of the Quran.

iq2.question: What is the primary theme of the first section (verses 1-14) of Surah At-Takwir?
options: Detailed laws of inheritance and marriage
The cataclysmic physical upheavals of the Day of Resurrection
Praising the historical battles of early Muslims
Instructions on daily prayer and fasting
iq2.explanation: The opening verses vividly describe cosmic disruptions such as the sun folding up, stars falling, mountains moving, and oceans blazing.

iq3.question: What pre-Islamic Arabian custom involving female children is specifically condemned and highlighted in verses 8-9?
options: Denying daughters the right to education
iq3.explanation: Verse 8-9 mention the buried female infant being asked for what sin she was slain, powerfully rebuking the jahiliyyah practice of infanticide.

iq4.question: According to Ibn Kathir, why is the buried infant questioned on the Day of Judgment?
options: To punish her for parental disobedience
To establish the utmost injustice done to her and to terrorize her murderer
To test her knowledge of scripture
To determine her placement in Purgatory
iq4.explanation: Asking the innocent victim highlights the magnitude of the crime and shocks the conscience of the perpetrators.

iq5.question: What oath does Allah swear in verses 15-16 using astronomical phenomena ('فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ')?
options: By the retreating, running, and hiding stars/planets
By the constellations of the zodiac
By the phases of the moon
iq5.explanation: Al-Khunnas and Al-Kunnas refer to celestial bodies that retreat during daylight and hide or sweep across their orbits.

iq6.question: How do verses 17-18 poetically describe night and dawn?
options: Night when it extends and dawn when it storms
Night when it departs/darkens (as'asa) and dawn when it breathes/brightens (tanaffasa)
Night when it freezes and dawn when it warms
Night when it is silent and dawn when it speaks
iq6.explanation: These vivid oaths emphasize the steady, majestic order of nature created by Allah.

iq7.question: To whom does 'رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ' (A noble messenger) refer in verse 19?
iq7.explanation: Exegetes agree that 'noble messenger' here refers to Angel Jibril, who brought the revelation from Allah.

iq8.question: What prestigious attributes are ascribed to Angel Jibril in verses 20-21?
options: Possessor of power, high rank with the Owner of the Throne, obeyed and trustworthy
Leader of earthly armies and treasurer of rain
Creator of celestial spheres and judge of nations
Companion of Adam and intercessor for mankind
iq8.explanation: Verses 20-21 highlight Jibril's supreme authority, station in the heavenly assembly, obedience among angels, and absolute trustworthiness.

iq9.question: How does verse 22 defend Prophet Muhammad ﷺ against the accusations of the Quraysh?
options: By declaring that he is a trained poet
By affirming 'And your companion is not mad (bimahnoon)'
By stating he is a wealthy king
By claiming he is an angel
iq9.explanation: The Quraysh accused the Prophet of being possessed by jinn or mad; Allah firmly refutes this slander.

iq10.question: Where did the Prophet ﷺ see Angel Jibril in his true angelic form, as mentioned in verse 23?
options: At the summit of Mount Sinai
iq10.explanation: Verse 23 states that the Prophet saw Jibril clearly on the open horizon.

iq11.question: What does 'وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ' (And he is not withholding concerning the unseen) mean regarding the Prophet ﷺ?
options: He hides revelation from his followers
He does not stingily withhold or alter the divine knowledge revealed to him
He charges money for teaching scripture
He predicts the future without divine permission
iq11.explanation: The Prophet faithfully conveys every part of the divine message without holding back or corrupting it.

iq12.question: How does verse 25 protect the Quran from being associated with demonic forces?
options: By stating it is protected by iron walls
By affirming 'And it is not the word of an expelled devil (shaytan rajeem)'
By forbidding it to be read at night
iq12.explanation: Pagans claimed the Quran was inspired by devils or poetry; Allah explicitly rejects this falsehood.

iq13.question: What profound rhetorical challenge is posed in verse 26 ('فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ')?
options: So where are you traveling for trade?
So where are you going in your disbelief after such clear proof?
So where will you hide from the army?
So where do souls migrate after death?
iq13.explanation: It challenges human intellect: having seen clear signs of truth, which misguided path could anyone possibly choose to follow?

iq14.question: How is the Quran characterized in verse 27 ('إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعَالَمِينَ')?
options: As a code of tribal law
As a reminder to all the worlds (mankind and jinn)
As a historical chronicle of Arabia
iq14.explanation: The Quran serves as a universal admonition and guidance for all creation.

iq15.question: What condition for receiving guidance is specified in verse 28 ('لِمَنْ شَاءَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ')?
options: Whoever among you wills to take the straight path / be steadfast
iq15.explanation: Guidance is available for whoever genuinely desires righteousness and alignment with truth.

iq16.question: What fundamental theological truth regarding human free will and divine sovereignty is established in verse 29 ('وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ')?
options: Human beings possess absolute independence from God
Human will operates within the overarching sovereign will and permission of Allah
Everything happens purely by random chance
iq16.explanation: While humans have moral agency and choice, nothing can happen in creation except by Allah's sovereign decree and will.

iq17.question: How does Surah At-Takwir conclude in verse 30?
options: With a warning of immediate earthly punishment
With the proclamation 'And you do not will except that Allah wills, the Lord of the worlds'
With a prayer for prophetic success
iq17.explanation: The surah ends by attributing all sovereignty, power, and lordship to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

iq18.question: What is the overarching connection between the first half of Surah At-Takwir and its second half?
options: One half discusses law, the other economics
The first half proves Allah's power over the physical universe on Judgment Day; the second half proves His authority over spiritual revelation
One half describes animals, the other angels
Both halves focus exclusively on the Battle of Badr
iq18.explanation: Both themes establish absolute divine power—over cosmic creation and over the preservation of His message.

iq19.question: In the context of Asbab al-Nuzul, what prompted the revelation of verses defending the Prophet ﷺ against madness?
options: The Prophet losing his voice during a speech
The Quraysh mocking him as majnoon (mad) and accusing him of sorcery when he recited the Quran
An attack by rival tribes in Taif
iq19.explanation: Meccan elites resorted to slander to deter people from listening to the Quran, prompting divine refutation.

iq20.question: What jurisprudential or ethical lesson is derived from the condemnation of female infanticide in Surah At-Takwir?
options: Strict legal prohibition of murder and the upholding of the sanctity of innocent human life
iq20.explanation: Islam eradicated barbaric pre-Islamic practices by establishing the sacred right to life for every human being, especially vulnerable children.

iq21.question: What does 'إِذَا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ' (When souls are paired) signify according to classical commentators?
options: Every person being reunited with their like-minded peers (righteous with righteous, wicked with wicked)
iq21.explanation: Ibn Kathir and others explain that souls are joined with their counterparts or their deeds (e.g., believers with Houris or fellow believers, wrongdoers with devils).

iq22.question: What does 'وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ' (When oceans are set ablaze) indicate about the final transformation of the earth?
options: Oceans being heated until they turn into raging fire or overflowing
Oceans turning into sweet drinking water
iq22.explanation: Sujjirat means ignited into fire or filled to overflowing due to the tremendous heat and cataclysm of the Last Hour.

iq23.question: Why are the stars described as 'انكَدَرَتْ' (inkadarat) in verse 2?
options: They lose their light, become dim, and fall scattered
iq23.explanation: Inkadarat denotes losing light and falling down from the firmament.

iq24.question: What is the significance of swearing by celestial phenomena ('وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا عَسْعَسَ وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ') in a Makkan surah?
options: To direct attention to the precision of cosmic creation as evidence of the Creator's majesty and truth of resurrection
To predict weather patterns for traders
iq24.explanation: Allah uses majestic signs of nature to validate the profound truth of His message.

iq25.question: How does Surah At-Takwir reinforce the doctrine of individual accountability ('عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا أَحْضَرَتْ')?
options: By stating that families share sins
By affirming that every soul will personally witness and recognize everything it prepared and brought forth
By delegating judgment to tribal leaders
iq25.explanation: On Judgment Day, nothing remains hidden; every soul confronts its own recorded deeds.

iq26.question: What does 'وَإِذَا الْجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ' (And when Paradise is brought near) signify for the believers?
options: Paradise is brought close so the righteous can witness and enter their ultimate reward
Paradise is moved to the earthly realm
iq26.explanation: Bringing Paradise near honors the believers and gladdens their hearts upon arrival.

iq27.question: What emotional impact was the vivid imagery of Surah At-Takwir intended to produce on its initial Meccan audience?
options: Awakening from heedlessness, fear of accountability, and realization of the gravity of the Hereafter
iq27.explanation: The apocalyptic descriptions shake listeners out of worldly distraction and focus their hearts on eternity.

iq28.question: In verse 10, when the scrolls are spread open ('وَإِذَا الصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ'), what do these scrolls contain?
options: The recorded deeds of every human being
iq28.explanation: The books of deeds compiled by recording angels are opened for public reckoning.

iq29.question: What does 'كُشِطَتْ' (kushitat) imply regarding the sky in verse 11 ('وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ كُشِطَتْ')?
options: It is stripped away or rolled back like a hide
iq29.explanation: Kushitat refers to removing or peeling back the sky, just as animal skin is stripped off.

iq30.question: Why is Angel Jibril described as 'أَمِينٍ' (Trustworthy) in verse 21?
options: Because he faithfully delivers Allah's revelation without omission, addition, or alteration
Because he guards the gates of Makkah
iq30.explanation: Trustworthiness is the essential qualification for conveying divine revelation intact.

iq31.question: What is the significance of the rhetorical question 'بِأَيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ' in highlighting social justice?
options: It champions the rights of the most defenseless members of society against brutal oppression
iq31.explanation: By centering the inquiry on an innocent murdered infant, the Quran establishes an unyielding moral stance against injustice.

iq32.question: How does Surah At-Takwir refute anyone claiming the Quran is authored by a human poet or sorcerer?
options: By challenging them to produce a similar surah
By describing the exalted angelic transmission through Jibril from the Lord of the worlds
iq32.explanation: The chain of custody—from Allah to Jibril to Muhammad ﷺ—proves its transcendent celestial origin.

iq33.question: What does 'مَكِينٍ' (Makeen) mean when describing Angel Jibril in verse 20?
options: Possessing high rank, authority, and established position with Allah
iq33.explanation: Makeen denotes high standing, prestige, and influence in the heavenly court.

iq34.question: Why does the surah emphasize human free will paired with divine sovereignty in the final verses?
options: To remind people that while they have the choice to seek the straight path, ultimate control and success belong solely to Allah
To prove stars control human destiny
iq34.explanation: It balances moral responsibility (whoever wills to be steadfast) with total dependence on Allah's will.

iq35.question: What is the overarching spiritual message of Surah At-Takwir for every reader?
options: Material wealth is the ultimate goal
The physical world is temporary, accountability is certain, and the Quran is divine truth guiding humanity to salvation
Astronomy is the only useful science
History repeats itself endlessly without purpose
iq35.explanation: The surah unites cosmic eschatology with prophetic truth to inspire sincere faith and righteous preparation for the Hereafter.

aq14.question: What is the root of the verb 'سُعِّرَتْ' (Su'irat - Ignited / made to blaze)?

aq15.question: What is the root of the verb 'أُزْلِفَتْ' (Uzlifat - Brought near)?

aq16.question: What is the root of the verb 'أَحْضَرَتْ' (Ahdarat - Brought / presented)?

aq18.question: What is the root of the word 'الْكُنَّسِ' (Al-Kunnas - The hiding / sweeping stars)?
